Plot a Changepoint Prediction

Source: R/autoplot.R
autoplot.PredictionCpt.Rd

Draws the facets of autoplot.TaskCpt() for the predicted sequences plus the segmentation decoded at each sequence's predicted penalty: dashed vertical lines at predicted changes (label_type = "changepoint") or horizontal segments at the mean count of each predicted peak (label_type = "peak"). For the 0changes, 1change, noPeaks and peaks labels, a mark missing from a region that requires one, or inside a region that forbids it, is a label error. peakStart and peakEnd regions are scored on where a peak starts or ends, not on overlap.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'PredictionCpt'
autoplot(
  object,
  task,
  type = "segmentation",
  Kmax = NULL,
  theme = ggplot2::theme_minimal(),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

(PredictionCpt).

task

(TaskCpt)
Task the prediction was made on; must contain every predicted row.

type

(character(1))
"segmentation" (default) draws the decoded marks; "roc" draws the ROC curve mlr_measures_changepoint.auc integrates, from penaltyLearning::ROChange(), with the AUC as title and a point at the predicted penalties (shift 0).

Kmax

(integer(1) | NULL)
Complexity cap for a prediction that does not record one; ignored when the prediction carries Kmax.

theme

(ggplot2::theme())
The ggplot2::theme_minimal() is applied by default.

...

(ignored).

Value

ggplot2::ggplot().

Details

A PredictionCpt stores only the predicted log(lambda) per sequence, so the segmentation is re-derived the way mlr_measures_changepoint.label_error does it: sequences and labels come from task, and the complexity cap from the Kmax the prediction records per sequence (learners of this package always record it). Kmax is only needed for a prediction built by hand without that record. A non-finite predicted penalty selects no model and raises an error, as do duplicated row ids (combined resampling iterations).

Every predicted row gets a facet; for many sequences predict on a subset (learner$predict(task, row_ids = rows)).

Examples

library(data.table)
set.seed(36)
toy = data.table(
  seq = list(c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9)), rnorm(100, 0)),
  label = list(
    data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = c("1change", "1change")),
    data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  )
)
task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = toy,
  target = "label", sequence = "seq", label_type = "changepoint"
)

p = PredictionCpt$new(task = task, response = c(2.5, 3.0))
# A hand-made prediction records no Kmax, so pass it; learner predictions carry their own.
ggplot2::autoplot(p, task = task, Kmax = 3L)

ggplot2::autoplot(p, task = task, type = "roc", Kmax = 3L)
